title: Saving resources through repeat-until-success positive-operator-valued-measure measurements in quantum computation
authors: Hefeng Wang, Sixia Yu, Hua Xiang
abstract: We present a quantum computation approach in which computation is guided by positive-operator-valuedmeasure (POVM) measurements following a given computation path in multisteps. In this approach, one ancillary qubit is coupled to a register of working qubits, and a POVM measurement is implemented effectively on the working qubits by applying a unitary operation on the whole system followed by a projective measurement performed on the ancillary qubit. Each step of the computation is a repeat-until-success procedure such that the desired state of the step is obtained deterministically on the working qubits via POVM measurements. The principle of deferred measurement states that measurements can always be moved from an intermediate stage of a quantum circuit to the end of the circuit without affecting the efficiency of the computation.We demonstrate that in our approach, by introducing intermediate measurements on the ancillary qubit in the computation process, both the number of qubits and unitary operations can be reduced polynomially, compared to the case where the intermediate measurements are deferred to the end of the computation. We also provide a method for implementation of the approach.
summary: This paper proposes a quantum computation scheme that uses intermediate Positive-Operator-Valued-Measure (POVM) measurements within a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) framework. By performing measurements step-by-step rather than accumulating them, the protocol achieves a polynomial reduction in the required number of qubits and unitary gates compared to standard methods. This demonstrates a significant resource optimization technique for quantum circuit design.
main_problem: The paper addresses the resource inefficiency in quantum computation when intermediate measurements are required during a multi-step process.
main_result: Implementing intermediate measurements using a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) POVM approach provides a polynomial reduction in required qubits and unitary operations compared to deferring all measurements to the end.
method: The core method involves structuring the computation path such that each step is realized as a probabilistic, repeat-until-success measurement on the working qubits, mediated by an ancillary qubit.
model_or_system: The model uses $n$ working qubits and one ancillary qubit. The POVM measurement is physically implemented by applying a controlled unitary operation on the whole system followed by a projective measurement on the ancillary qubit.
key_observables: Success probability ($P_{	ext{succ}}$), number of required qubits, and count of unitary operations (e.g., Toffoli gates).
important_parameters: The success probability $p_k$ of each step, and the time evolution parameters ($t_k$) used in the Quantum Resonance Transfer (QRT) method.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the principle of deferred measurement and assumes that the overlap between adjacent states and the energy gap are polynomially large for the QRT implementation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum circuit for the RUS-POVM process (Fig. 1) and compare it conceptually to the circuit where intermediate measurements are deferred to the end (Fig. 2/3).
paper_structure: The paper details the RUS-POVM approach (Sec. II), its physical implementation via the QRT method (Sec. III), error analysis (Sec. IV), and a direct comparison of resource scaling against deferred measurement protocols (Sec. V).
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, resource-saving protocol for implementing complex quantum algorithms by strategically placing measurements, which is crucial for scaling quantum computation beyond idealized models.
